questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

No sooner did I come out of my home to go to the market when it started raining heavily which drenched me completely.

options.text: No sooner did I come out of my home

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**when it started raining heavily**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'than it started raining heavily' **should be there in place of **'when it started raining heavily'**
 
• If the second event occurs immediately after the first, we can express that idea using the structure no sooner … than.
 
• Note that in this structure no sooner introduces the event that occurred first.
 
 
• **​Examples: **No sooner had I arrived at the station than the train came.

 No sooner had we heard the noise than we rushed to the spot.
 
 
 
• Note that did is also possible in this structure.
 
 
• ​**Example: **No sooner did I arrive at the station than the train came
 
 

**Hence, the sentence can be correctly rewritten as:** *No sooner did I come out of my home to go to market **than** it started raining heavily which drenched me completely.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with a blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Fourteen kilometres ______, not a short distance, to reach to my office daily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e. 'is'. 

‘Fouteen kilometres’ is a collective noun (plural) and with it we will use singular verb form thus, ‘is’ should be used. For eg. The band is very popular, in this sentence, ‘band’ is plural and with it ‘is’ is used which is singular. Moreover, ‘has’, ‘have’ do not make any sense if fitted into the blank.

Hence, the sentence can be rewritten as, Fourteen kilometres is not a short distance, to reach to my office daily.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Petrify
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "Harden".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Petrify"** means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think, or it can mean to change organic matter into a stony substance. (भयभीत करना या काठ बना देना)

 
 
• **Example: **The horror movie was enough to petrify even the bravest viewer.
 
 
 
• **"Harden"** means to make or become hard or harder. (सख्त करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The lava will harden into rock within a few hours.
 
 
 
• In a broader sense, both "Petrify" and "Harden" involve making something stiff, rigid, or unyielding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Harden**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Adorn** (सजाना): To decorate or add beauty to something.

 
 
• **Example:** They adorn the hall with flowers for the wedding.
 
 
 
• **Calm** (शांत): To make someone or something less agitated or excited.
 
 
• **Example: **She took deep breaths to calm herself before speaking.
 
 
 
• **Curious** (जिज्ञासु): Eager to know or learn something.
 
 
• **Example:** The child was curious about the new toy.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

I had (a few) eggs in the fridge, so we need to go to the market to buy them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e. few.

‘A few’ means ‘some’ and has a positive connotation attached with it. In the given sentence, the speaker is highlighting a negative connotation that there are none or not many eggs left so they must be bought. Thus, ‘few’ has a negative connotation attached to it and captures the meaning of the given sentence in the most appropriate manner, it is the appropriate answer choice. 

Hence, the sentence can be correctly rewritten as, I had few eggs in the fridge, so we need to go to the market to buy them.Rest of the options are irrelevant and can be rejected.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

My brother is indifferent (about) whatever I say.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. to. 

The usage of ‘about’ with the adjective ‘indifferent’ is wrong in the above sentence. ‘indifferent’ is always followed by ‘to’, i.e. ‘indifferent to or indifferent towards something or someone’. Thus, the appropriate correction is the usage of ‘to’ instead of ‘about’. Rest of the options are vague and can be eliminated.

Hence, the sentence can be correctly rewritten as, My brother is indifferent to whatever I say.

questions.question:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P-But he did not know how to find one at that hour.

Q-It was his first visit to the city and he didn't know where to go.

R-Mohanlal's train was late and it reached Kolkata a little after midnight.

S-He thought he would go to a choultry where he would not have to pay rent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RQSP.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **R **introduces a general, independent idea. P, Q and S cannot be used to start the paragraph as they contain ‘he’, ‘his’ and ‘he’ respectively and only** R gives the answer to ‘he’ and ‘his’. Thus, R is the first sentence.**
 
• **Q logically follows R** by highlighting his trip to Kolkata that it was his first trip there.
 
• After reaching Kolkata for the first time, he wanted to go to a choultry, and thus, **sentence S is next in the sequence.**
 
• **Sentence P sums up the entire paragraph** and logically follows the previous three sentences.

**Hence, the sentence can be correctly rearranged as:** *Mohanlal's train was late and it reached Kolkata a little after midnight. It was his first visit to the city and he didn't know where to go. He thought he would go to a choultry where he would not have to pay rent. But he did not know how to find one at that hour.*

questions.question:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P-And slowly, you reach the pinnacle of self-awareness, experiencing a unity with all life.

Q-If you transform your energy positively, it naturally becomes compassion and love.

R-Once you experientially are a part of everything then nobody needs to teach you morality.

S-Then you can do something to improve the situation, but without anger.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**QPRS**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, or the starting of an incident
 
• Part Q will be the first sentence because the sentence 'transforming of energy positively, resulting in compassion and love *'* is a universal fact and it is an independent general statement. 
 
• **Part P **mentions the later results of transforming energy positively.
 
• **R further highlights the fact that when one experiences everything** then nobody needs to teach you morality.
 
• **S concludes the paragraph** and logically follows the statements preceding it.

**Hence, the sentence can be correctly arranged as: ***If you transform your energy positively, it naturally becomes compassion and love, and slowly, you reach the pinnacle of self-awareness, experiencing a unity with all life. Once you experientially are a part of everything then nobody needs to teach you morality then you can do something to improve the situation, but without anger.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• Once we get the idea that Q is the starting statement, we can mark our answer as option 2 as there is no other option starting from Q.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

Ram was singing a beautiful song for his mother.

options.text: A beautiful song was being sung by Ram for his mother.
A beautiful song was sang by Ram for his mother.
A beautiful song was sung by Ram for his mother.
A beautiful song was sung for his mother by Ram.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e. A beautiful song was being sung by Ram for his mother. 

While conversion from active to passive or vice-versa object and subject are interchanged. The correct past participle form of ‘sing’ is ‘sung’. Option 1 grammatically follows the idea as in the sentence it is mentioned that ‘Ram is singing’ i.e. the action is still occurring and has not ended yet. Only option 1, takes into consideration that the action is still going on as ‘being sung’ highlights that the action is still alive. Other options are vague and can be rejected.
